thread.title: Apple's (AAPL) 2018 Worldwide Developer Conference: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Apple's (AAPL) 2018 Worldwide Developer Conference: What to Expect
text:
iStock photo
Apple’s ( AAPL ) annual Worldwide Developer Conference (WWDC) kicks off Monday at the McEnery Convention Center in San Jose, California.
The week-long event — which runs from June 5 through 8 — begins Monday (1:00 p.m. EDT) with a keynote address from CEO Tim Cook. The Cupertino tech giant will host members of the media and thousands of app developers for discussions on various topics ranging from latest updates to its many software platforms (MacOS, iOS, WatchOS, etc.) to potentially new hardware releases and update to the company’s augmented reality (AR) and artificial intelligence (AI) initiatives.
Apple shares, which closed at an all-time high Friday at $190.24, have risen 12.4% year to date. The stock has returned 11% since the release of its second quarter earnings results on May 1 and is now less than 7% away from a $1 trillion market cap — considered a holy grail valuation . Over the past year, the race for that $1 trillion title has been between Apple, Amazon ( AMZN ), Google parent Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) and, more recently , Microsoft ( MSFT ). And if Apple plays its cards right this week at the WWDC, the race could be over.
Software: iOS and MacOS
Apple is broadly expected to unveil its latest iPhone operating system, dubbed iOS 12, from the current iteration of 11.4. It was at last year’s WWDC Apple launched iOS 11. And we expect Apple to stick to this current schedule. But unlike previous releases, iOS 12 is expected to have a cross-platform development feature that enables developers of mobile apps to easily create apps for Macs too.
Essentially, this move, according to Bloomberg , gives developers more incentive to create apps for the Mac line. And it may result in the iOS and MacOS merging through their apps. It goes without saying that Apple fans, especially those who are hardcore Mac users, will celebrate this feature, especially as the operating systems updates is expected to come with stability and performance improvements as well.
As part of the new operating system, Apple is also rumored to be pushing new initiatives towards "Digital Health,” which includes tools that lets users know how much time they spend on their iPhones and which apps they use the most. It other words, Apple’s Digital Health will let you know if you are, in fact, addicted to Facebook ( FB ), your Twitter ( TWTR ) feed, or your favorite video game. These tools are a response to concerns about smartphone addiction , which prompted Google to take a similar approach last month at its I/O developer conference.
Siri, AI and AR
The spotlight is also expected to be on artificial intelligence and augmented reality, which has become a new battleground growth area, where Google and Amazon are believed to be well ahead of Apple — particularly with voice-controlled home systems. Since its debut in 2011, Siri has taken a backseat to Alexa and Google Home assistant, which have become more prominent in their functionality. As such, I expect Siri to get a nice upgrade and become smarter .
Fans may also get an update on Apple’s ambitions in AI and AR — an area where Apple has invested heavily over the past couple of years. In April the company hired John Giannandrea, who previously served as Google’s chief of search and artificial intelligence, to run its “machine learning and A.I. strategy.” This hire was considered by most to be a major coup in Apple’s bid to outdo Google and Amazon.
It’s not known what Apple will release on Monday in relation to AI and AR, but the company’s new line of iPads, which features upgraded sensors and cameras to offer an improved AR experience, could be the backbone to its architecture and the company’s augmented reality ARKit. According to Bloomberg, the new iteration, dubbed ARKit 2.0, will add the ability for multiplayer AR games on separate devices, which means two players will be able to see the same AR scenario occurring through their phones’ displays.
Hardware
There are also rumors that Apple, which has dabbled in AR/VR smart glasses , may tease us with the software that will power the hardware. Speaking of hardware, Apple could also refresh the company's line of MacBooks and iPads and possibly AirPods. While I don’t expect Apple to say anything about the new iPhones or line of Apple Watch until its September event, I wouldn’t be surprised if the company surprised fans with a “one more thing” unveiling.
Suffice it to say, there will be plenty to talk about during the the WWDC, which you can live stream here . From an investment perspective, Apple shares have shown a tendency to sell off on the days of the WWDC as the market often takes a “sell the news” approach. Investors who are waiting for a better entry point in AAPL stock should watch the shares closely heading into the close Monday.
